new_statements.quote: Stress is not contrastive in Varli. In disyllabic and trisyllabic words it falls on the first syllable; in four syllable words on the second syllable and in five syllable words on the first with secondary stress on the penultimate syllable. /oː.ɖhiː/ [ˈoː.ɖhiː] 'this much' /bha.kə.ɾiː/ [ˈbha.kə.ɾiː] 'bread' /da.da.gi.ɾiː/ [da.ˈda.gi.ɾiː] 'trouble' /no.kə.ɾiː.ʋa.ɭa/ [ˈno.kə.ɾiː.ˈʋa.ɭa] 'one who has a job'

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (113 pp., pdfinfo author "G. Abraham and Hemalatha Abraham", title "Varli Phonological and Grammar") and re-extracted PDF pp. 40-42 with extracted text. Section "4.5. Stress" is at the foot of PDF p. 41 and reads exactly: "Stress is not contrastive in Varli. In disyllabic and trisyllabic words it falls on the first syllable; in four syllable words on the second syllable and in five syllable words on the first with secondary stress on the penultimate syllable." The four transcribed examples open PDF p. 42: /oː.ɖhiː/ [ˈoː.ɖhiː] 'this much'; /bha.kə.ɾiː/ [ˈbha.kə.ɾiː] 'bread'; /da.da.gi.ɾiː/ [da.ˈda.gi.ɾiː] 'trouble'; /no.kə.ɾiː.ʋa.ɭa/ [ˈno.kə.ɾiː.ˈʋa.ɭa] 'one who has a job'. new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive and predictable from syllable count: initial in two- and three-syllable words, on the second syllable in four-syllable words, and initial (with a secondary stress on the penult) in five-syllable words. Initial stress is the dominant pattern; the four-syllable case is the one deviation, and the sole four-syllable example (da.ˈda.gi.ɾiː) is a loan/compound-like form, so the reading is fixed-initial with a count-conditioned exception rather than weight-sensitive.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Stated only for five-syllable words: secondary stress on the penultimate syllable, e.g. [ˈno.kə.ɾiː.ˈʋa.ɭa] 'one who has a job'.
new_statements.exceptions: Four-syllable words take stress on the second syllable ([da.ˈda.gi.ɾiː] 'trouble'); no other exceptions or weight/length effects are mentioned, although the language has phonemic vowel length.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word, citation forms (isolated lexical items); no phrase-level statement. Data from Khedpa village, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, collected from 1995 by SIL-affiliated missionaries; the sketch is short and gives four examples only.
new_statements.identity_note: The SIL sketch (Abraham & Abraham 2012) describes Varli as spoken at Khedpa village, Dadra & Nagar Haveli (the authors' Dogri/Davri dialect area), i.e. the Dadra & Nagar Haveli / Dungar (hill) Varli that Glottolog The earlier scan's named source (Grierson LSI IX.III) contains no Varli sketch; the LSI Varli specimen is in Vol. VII (Marathi) pp. 141 ff. and is silent on stress.
